out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: sliced tomatoes (52F) stored in front refrigerated preptable. Sliced tomatoes overfilled in deep metal container.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM relocated sliced tomatoes back to walk in refrigerator to cool to 41F or below. CFM agreed to reduce amount of sliced tomatoes stored in metal container. CFM agreed to use shallow pan to facilitate better cold holding in the front refrigerated preptable.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. CDI: EHS will email manager copy of employee health policy to review information with staff, sign, and maintain on file for future reference.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS will. Email manager copy of written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at hand sinks inside the men’s and women’s restrooms shared with food service employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. CDI: EHS will email manager copy of handwashing signs to print and place at hand sinks inside the men’s and women’s restroom.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: sliced tomatoes inside of walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CDI: staff member date marked the sliced tomatoes with expiration date.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS DISCUSSED HAND WASHING WITH THE MANAGER AND STAFF MEMBER WAS OBSERVED HAND WASHING AFTER INSTRUCTIONS WERE PROVIDED.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: Observed the hot water at both hand sinks at 84f-87f.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO INCREASE THE TEMPERATURE OF THE TANKLESS WATER HEATER AND ENSURE THE HAND SINKS REACH 100F. SEND PROOF OF PROPER HOT WATER TEMPERATURE NO LATER THAN 6/2/2025.

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at the WOMEN’S restroom hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO PROVIDE PAPER TOWELS.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at RESTROOM handwashing sink(s) used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO PROVIDE HAND WASHING SIGNAGE IN RESTROOM(S) AS NEEDED BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) RAW BACON IMPROPERLY STORED ON A SHELF INSIDE THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS HAD THE MANAGER MOVE THE RAW BACON TO THE LOWEST SHELF IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO PREVENT ANY POSSIBLE CROSS CONTAMINATION.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed dish soap stored on shelving units above the 3-vat sink where clean equipment is stored.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO STORE THE CHEMICALS AND DETERGENTS BELOW AND SEPARATED FROM CLEAN EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS, FOOD, AND CLEAN LINENS.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Observed spray bottle(s) of chemicals or sanitizers unlabeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO ENSURE ALL WORKING BOTTLES OF CHEMICALS AND SANITIZERS ARE LABELED AT ALL TIMES.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: 1) SPRAY BOTTLE OF WATER, 2) BULK BINS OF SUGAR AND CORN MEAL.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO PROPERLY LABEL ALL WORKING CONTAINERS OF FOODS BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Openings to the exterior of the building are present along the BASE OF THE FRONT DOOR.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO SEAL THE BASE OF THE FRONT DOOR USING A DOOR SWEEP TO PREVENT POSSIBLE ENTRY OF INSECTS/RODENTS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed food stored on the floor in the kitchen areas, walk-in refrigerator, and walk-in freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO ORGANIZE THE SPACE MORE EFFECTIVELY SO THAT ALL FOOD AND BEVERAGES ARE STORED ON NSF APPROVED SHELVING UNITS OR DUNNAGE RACKS BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EHS DISCUSSED WITH MANAGEMENT THAT ONLY CLEAN, DRY TOWELS MAY BE SITTING ON WORK SURFACES. WET TOWELS ARE REQUIRED TO BE IN A QUATERNARY AMMONIA SANITIZING SOLUTION AT 200-400PPM AND DIRTY TOWELS ARE REQUIRED TO BE IN LAUNDRY. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed boxes of single service items stored in direct contact with the floor in the kitchen areas.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EHS DISCUSSED WITH MANAGEMENT TO ORDER A NSF APPROVED DUNNAGE RACK AND ORGANIZE THE SPACE EFFECTIVELY SO THAT ALL ITEMS ARE OFF THE FLOOR BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Manual Wash Water Temperature
violations.observation: Observed the hot water at the 3-vat sink not getting above 104f.
violations.corrective_action: The temperature of the wash solution for manual warewashing machine must be no less than 110F or the temperature specified on the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO SET THE TANKLESS WATER HEATER TO 140F AND ENSURE A MINIMUM HOT WATER TEMPERATURE AT THE 3–VAT SINK OF 110F. SEND PROOF OF CORRECTION NO LATER THAN 6/2/2025. JERSEY MIKE'S SUBS (Inspection Date: 05/23/2025) Page 2 of 4
